overview.title: What is The Duskbloods?
paragraphs: The Duskbloods is a multiplayer action game developed by FromSoftware and directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, creators of Elden Ring and the Dark Souls series. It is published by Nintendo as a Switch 2 exclusive and is scheduled for release in 2026.

Set during the Twilight of Humanity — the twilight of human civilization — players take on the role of the Bloodsworn: warriors who have gained superhuman power through special blood. They compete for the First Blood, a mysterious force that drives the game's central conflict.

Matches bring together up to eight players in PvPvE battles that blend competition between players with fights against powerful enemies. Each Bloodsworn has unique weapons, abilities, and a customizable blood history that shapes their path and destiny across the fight.

items.title: 8-Player PvPvE Combat
items.desc: Every match pits up to eight Bloodsworn against each other and against formidable enemies simultaneously, blending rivalry and cooperation in unpredictable ways.

items.title: The Bloodsworn
items.desc: More than a dozen playable characters, each with distinct weapons, abilities, and appearance. Every Bloodsworn carries a blood history you can shape to influence their path.

items.title: Blood Powers
items.desc: Special blood grants abilities that transcend human limits. Master these powers to turn the tide of battle and pursue the First Blood.

items.title: Twilight of Humanity
items.desc: A dark, romantic world moving from gothic Victorian streets toward an industrial modern era — the end stage of civilization as a stage for conflict.

items.title: FromSoftware Design
items.desc: Directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, The Duskbloods channels the studio's signature dark-fantasy craft into a fresh multiplayer direction, developed by a dedicated team.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Exclusive
items.desc: FromSoftware's first console-exclusive title in over twenty years, built from the ground up for Nintendo Switch 2 hardware.

networkBanner.title: Network Test Applications Closed
networkBanner.desc: The application period for The Duskbloods closed network test has ended. Selected players were notified on August 7. The network test runs August 21–23.

charactersTeaser.title: Fighters bound by blood
charactersTeaser.desc: Step into the role of the Bloodsworn — more than a dozen playable warriors, each with unique weapons, abilities, and a personal blood history. Not mindless monsters, but conscious, dominant fighters with their own identity and destiny.

items.q: When does The Duskbloods release?
items.a: The Duskbloods is scheduled for release in 2026 on Nintendo Switch 2. FromSoftware and its parent company Kadokawa have confirmed the title is still on track for a 2026 launch, though a precise release date has not been announced.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive?
items.a: Yes. The Duskbloods is published by Nintendo and is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2. It is FromSoftware's first console-exclusive title in more than twenty years.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods multiplayer only?
items.a: The Duskbloods is built around 8-player PvPvE multiplayer as its core, but it has also been confirmed to include a single-player mode, so solo players can experience the game as well.

items.q: Who is developing The Duskbloods?
items.a: The Duskbloods is developed by FromSoftware and directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, the president of FromSoftware and director of Elden Ring and the Dark Souls series. It is published by Nintendo.

items.q: How do I join the network test?
items.a: Registration for the closed network test was held through the official site, with results sent to players. The test runs on Nintendo Switch 2. Check our network test page for the schedule, preload details, and what to expect.

items.q: Does The Duskbloods support crossplay?
items.a: Because The Duskbloods is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2, crossplay with other platforms is not applicable. Multiplayer takes place among Switch 2 players.

intro.title: How to Play The Duskbloods
intro.lead: The Duskbloods is an action RPG built around 8-player PvPvE multiplayer matches. Here's how combat, characters, and match flow come together.

sections.title: PvPvE matches for up to 8 players
sections.desc: Each match brings together up to eight Bloodsworn. PvPvE means player-versus-player-versus-environment: you compete against other players while also facing powerful enemies, so every fight is a three-way contest of rivalry, opportunism, and survival.

sections.title: The Bloodsworn and their blood powers
sections.desc: Players take on the role of the Bloodsworn — humans who have gained superhuman abilities through special blood. These blood powers let fighters transcend ordinary human limits, defining how each character plays and how they pursue the First Blood at the heart of the conflict.

sections.title: A dozen-plus playable characters
sections.desc: More than a dozen Bloodsworn are available, each with distinctive weapons, abilities, and appearance, plus room to customize your build. Every character carries a blood history that influences their path and destiny across a match.

sections.title: The First Blood and the Twilight of Humanity
sections.desc: The setting is the Twilight of Humanity — the end stage of civilization. Within it flows the First Blood, a mysterious force the Bloodsworn compete to obtain. This pursuit is the engine that drives every match and the game's overarching conflict.

sections.title: Solo play and cooperation
sections.desc: While multiplayer is the core, The Duskbloods also includes a single-player mode. Cooperative elements have been discussed for the full release, so both solo and group play are part of the experience.

sections.title: FromSoftware's craft, a new direction
sections.desc: Directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and built by a dedicated team, The Duskbloods channels FromSoftware's dark-fantasy design language into a fresh multiplayer format — without interfering with the studio's single-player lineup, which continues in parallel.

roles.title: Bloodsworn Roles & Builds
roles.desc: Each Bloodsworn offers distinct weapons and abilities, and your blood history shapes their path. Experiment with different characters and loadouts to find the fighter that fits your style.

items.title: Weapons
items.desc: Every Bloodsworn wields signature weapons that define their range, pace, and approach to combat.

items.title: Abilities
items.desc: Blood powers grant moves and skills that go beyond human limits, opening offensive and defensive options.

items.title: Blood History
items.desc: A customizable narrative element that influences your character's path and destiny through the match.

matchStructure.title: Dusk Battle Match Flow
matchStructure.desc: Eight Bloodsworn are summoned to the human dusk to compete for the First Blood. Battles are divided into 4 phases, with the Grail progressively culling until the final 3 survivors compete for the Blood Bestowal.

stages.name: Phase I: Exploration and Conquest
stages.desc: Eight Bloodsworn enter the Lands of Dusk and begin accumulating Virtue.
bullets: Defeat enemies, light lantern corpses for Flame Virtue, explore for items
Regional features appear — Bloodbag Elders, Alchemy Furnaces, Kin Small Circles
Earn Repulsion Virtue by defeating great foes or trespassers
Collect items to increase Collector Commendation

stages.name: Phase II: Ritual Sites and Culling
stages.desc: The Grail begins its culling. Bloodsworn with insufficient Virtue are eliminated. Ritual sites open.
bullets: Two Virtue types at ritual sites: Sword Virtue (defeat Bloodsworn) and Pledge Virtue (swear to pillars)
Claim Redstones (boost Sword Virtue) or Goldstones (boost Pledge Virtue) from rock plinths
Leaving a ritual site after entering penalizes you with HP loss
Random events trigger: zeppelin support fire, magnetic storms

stages.name: Phase III: Events and Intensifying Battle
stages.desc: Culling continues. Regional features change. The battlefield grows more dangerous.
bullets: Regional features change, offering new enhancement opportunities
Ritual sites reopen with even fiercer competition
Random events continue to affect the battlefield
Accumulate Blood Powers and grow your kin to prepare for the final phase

stages.name: Final Phase: Moon's Blood Bestowal
stages.desc: Only the three Bloodsworn with the highest Virtue remain. They fight for the ultimate victory.
bullets: The Grail grants two lives — you can revive once
Bonus HP based on accumulated Virtue from previous phases
Alliances dissolve — former allies become opponents
Use your Bloodsworn, kin powers, and items to claim victory

matchStructure.finalDetail: Only the tear of the moon falls for one. Use the Bloodsworn, kin powers, and items you've honed in earlier phases to become the last victor.

systems.title: Leveling Up Bloodsworn
systems.desc: You can earn experience and level up by defeating enemies and other players, increasing HP and attack power.

systems.title: Compacts with Kin
systems.desc: Those who have entered an agreement with the Order of Dusk are known as kin.

systems.title: Powers of Blood
systems.desc: Acquired by defeating great foes or trespassers — choose one of two options each time. Up to 5 Powers of Blood can be manifested at once; swap them from the menu.

systems.title: Regional Features
systems.desc: Regional features change each phase: Bloodbag Elders (Bloodsworn Skill enhancement), Alchemy Furnaces (weapon enhancement), Kin Small Circles (kin EXP), and exploration items such as the Fire Flask and Memorial Stake.

mechanics.title: Staggering
mechanics.desc: Attacking an enemy fills the stagger gauge. Max out the gauge to stagger enemies and create a significant opportunity.

mechanics.title: Drinking Blood
mechanics.desc: Suck the blood of staggered enemies, inflicting large damage while recovering HP. Weaker foes will be spellbound and follow you.

mechanics.title: Howling
mechanics.desc: All Bloodsworn can howl, producing a gust of wind. Howl in time with an enemy's attack to interrupt it and greatly increase their stagger gauge. Can deflect some ranged attacks.

mechanics.title: Guard
mechanics.desc: Generate a shield to block frontward attacks. Works in the air. Repeated attacks will break the shield. Broken shields auto-repair. Press R after guarding for a Guard Counter.

mechanics.title: Golden Blood Stake
mechanics.desc: Restores HP. Replenish uses by defeating enemies or finding Golden Blood in the world.

items.title: Alliances
items.desc: You can form alliances with rival Bloodsworn. Petition other Bloodsworn you encounter for an alliance.

items.title: Sigils
items.desc: Sigils establish relationships with other Bloodsworn. When a Sigil is etched, a unique objective appears, and completing it earns you Virtue. The network test version includes four Sigils: Sigil of a Sworn Enemy; Sigil of an Old Friend; Sigil of the Eye of Muralis; Sigil of Love Ephemeral. In the release version, they are planned to become freely changeable.

hub.title: House of Night
hub.desc: The base of the Bloodsworn. You can choose which Bloodsworn to use or learn basic controls and rules.

features.name: Battle Remembrance
features.desc: You can experience parts of Dusk Battles and learn the rules. Once you visit the House of Night, it's recommended that you first try experiencing the battle from this menu.

features.name: Archive
features.desc: Information recorded here can be reviewed at any time, including tutorials, Bloodsworn weapons, the kin you've entered a compact with, items, Powers of Blood, and events.

features.name: Courtyard
features.desc: In the House of Night's courtyard, you can practice controls on the Graveyard Scarecrow or try out Bloodsworn actions. You can also change various settings from the menu.

features.name: Game Rules
features.desc: In the Dusk Battle menu, you can configure matchmaking. Standard (default), No Alliances, or Bloodbound Alliances. In Bloodbound, all Bloodsworn battle in pairs — the alliance persists into the final phase.

virtue.title: Virtue System Explained
virtue.desc: Virtue is needed to survive Dusk Battles. Only the Bloodsworn with the highest Virtue in the second and third phases survive the culling. Virtue can be obtained not just through battle, but also through exploration and strategy.

types.title: Repulsion Virtue
types.desc: Within the Lands of Dusk, there are great foes. These are stronger even than other enemies. Then there are even greater outside threats called trespassers.

types.title: Flame Virtue
types.desc: Flame Virtue can be obtained by lighting flames within the skulls of corpses sitting on chairs scattered around the Lands of Dusk. There are lantern corpses that are a degree larger.

types.title: Sword Virtue
types.desc: You can get Sword Virtue by defeating other Bloodsworn at ritual sites. This Virtue is not earned outside of ritual sites.

types.title: Pledge Virtue
types.desc: Blood pledge pillars can be found within each ritual site. Swear to them to earn Pledge Virtue. This Virtue is lost if the pledge is overwritten by another Bloodsworn.

types.title: Commendation Virtue
types.desc: There are two types of Commendations, and the players with the highest and second-highest values for each of these can earn Virtue at the end of each phase.

events.title: Events
events.desc: In Phase II and Phase III, there may be events that change the Lands of Dusk.

items.title: Events
items.desc: In Phase II and Phase III, there may be events that change the Lands of Dusk. There may be unexpected developments, such as a zeppelin appearing in the sky from which you can request supporting fire, or a powerful storm that forcefully transports players to other locations.

items.title: Magnetic Storm
items.desc: A powerful magnetic storm appears, forcefully transporting players to other locations.

bloodPowers.title: Powers of Blood
bloodPowers.desc: Defeat great foes or trespassers to acquire Powers of Blood, granting various abilities. Select one from multiple options. Up to 5 can be manifested at once, adjustable via menu.

coopBattle.title: Co-op Battles
coopBattle.desc: When battling a trespasser, nearby Bloodsworn are invited to join forces. Fight together with those who accept.

regions.title: Exploring Regions
regions.desc: Each region of the Lands of Dusk has different features per phase. Check the map for features that suit your play style.

features.title: Bloodbag Elder
features.desc: Bloodbag Elders appear. Defeat them to earn Blood Crystals for enhancing Bloodsworn arts.

features.title: Alchemy Furnace
features.desc: Alchemy Furnaces appear, granting elemental attributes to weapons. Matching attributes upgrades the weapon.

features.title: Kin Small Circle
features.desc: Kin Small Circles appear, strengthening your compact and granting large EXP to contracted kin.

features.title: Exploration Items
features.desc: Obtain items through exploration or defeating enemies. Molotov cocktails burn fiercely, Life Gravestones let you revive at their location.

items.title: Lock-on Target Priority
items.desc: In game options, set whether to prioritize enemies attacking you when switching lock-on targets. Default is OFF.

items.title: Info Screen
items.desc: Press [+] during Dusk Battles to view the map, your position, other Bloodsworn traces, and regional features.

items.title: Warp
items.desc: Select warp points on the map to travel far distances. Cannot be used: at phase start, shortly after warping/reviving, or during combat.

items.title: Trespasser Location
items.desc: Trespassers are shown on the map with special markers. Even stronger trespassers also exist.

items.title: Gestures
items.desc: Hold [+] to open the gesture menu. Some gesture actions are key to completing certain Sigil objectives.

items.title: Function Menu
items.desc: Hold [Y] to open the function menu. Includes: Alliance Requests, Placing Markers, Observation Mode, Summoning Kin.

meta.title: Game Mechanics | The Duskbloods Guide
meta.desc: Deep dive into The Duskbloods core mechanics: Dusk Battle flow, Virtue system, combat mechanics, kin compacts, and more.

stones.title: Red & Gold Stones Guide
stones.desc: Claim Redstones and Goldstones from rock plinths at ritual sites. Only one type at a time — Redstones boost Sword Virtue, Goldstones boost Pledge Virtue. Choose based on your play style.

items.title: Redstone
items.desc: While holding a Redstone, earn more Sword Virtue at ritual sites. Suited for aggressive players.

items.title: Goldstone
items.desc: While holding a Goldstone, earn more Pledge Virtue. Suited for players who prefer to avoid combat.

items.q: How many players are in a Duskbloods match?
items.a: Each Dusk Battle match supports up to 8 players competing in PvPvE combat. Players fight against each other and against AI-controlled enemies simultaneously.

items.q: What is PvPvE in The Duskbloods?
items.a: PvPvE means Player versus Player versus Environment. In The Duskbloods, you compete against other Bloodsworn while also fighting powerful AI enemies, bosses, and environmental hazards across the map.

items.q: What are the Bloodsworn roles?
items.a: The Bloodsworn are playable characters with unique weapons and abilities. Each role offers a different playstyle — melee-focused fighters, ranged attackers, and support-oriented builds. Your Blood History further customizes your character's path.

items.q: How does the Virtue system work?
items.a: Virtue is a progression mechanic that enhances your Bloodsworn during a match. Different Virtue types provide passive bonuses and unlock new abilities as you progress through the Dusk Battle.

items.q: What are Red Stones and Gold Stones?
items.a: Red Stones and Gold Stones are collectible items found at Ritual Sites on the map. They provide powerful buffs and upgrades to your Bloodsworn during a match.

items.q: How do I join The Duskbloods network test?
items.a: Register through the Nintendo eShop on your Switch 2. The closed network test runs in 2026. Check our Network Test page for exact dates and registration details.

roster.title: Bloodsworn
roster.desc: The Network Test features 6 playable Bloodsworn, each with unique weapons and Bloodsworn Skills.

items.name: Albert

bloodArts.name: Blood Blade
bloodArts.desc: Fires off a blade formed of the wielder's blood. Scales with wielder's blood caliber.

bloodArts.name: Light of Hayern
bloodArts.desc: Raises the crystal of light mounted on the casing and shines forth a beam of light.

powers.name: High Lorrik Blood
powers.desc: Blood-based Bloodsworn skills have additional usages.

powers.name: Upriser
powers.desc: Increases stagger potential of attacks against Bloodsworn with high Virtue.

items.tagline: A jeweled saber and an SMG — flex between clean melee pressure and mid-range finishers.
playstyle: Albert is the roster’s most approachable all-rounder. Lorrik’s Jeweled Saber rewards clean spacing and stagger play, while the Submachine Gun lets you harass or confirm kills without committing to a full melee approach.

His kit scales with blood caliber, so early Virtue and Blood upgrades feel immediately stronger. Blood Blade is a reliable poke; Light of Hayern is the burst tool when a target is staggered or pinned.

tips.title: Bank Virtue early
tips.desc: High Lorrik Blood grants extra uses of blood-based skills — more Virtue and blood pickups mean more Blades and beams per fight.

tips.title: Hunt high-Virtue targets
tips.desc: Upriser increases stagger against Bloodsworn who are already winning. Steal their momentum instead of farming weak players.

tips.title: Saber for stagger, SMG for confirms
tips.desc: Open with melee to fill the stagger gauge, then swap to the SMG when they try to disengage.

lore: Albert carries the jeweled saber of House Lorrik and a modern sidearm — a walking argument that the Twilight of Humanity still mixes aristocratic bloodline with industrial firepower.
His Aspects (High Lorrik Blood, Upriser) read like a revolutionary’s manifesto: more power from blood craft, and extra pressure against those already crowned by Virtue.

items.name: Bloodhand Jan

bloodArts.name: Blink
bloodArts.desc: Uses the wielder's blood to enhance the speed of evasion. Effect will be lost after some time.

bloodArts.name: Surrender to My Blood
bloodArts.desc: Quench the axe's thirst with the wielder's blood, strike the blade into the ground and rend the surrounding area with blood slashes.

powers.name: Bloodhand Lineage
powers.desc: Counterattacking after receiving damage restores HP.

powers.name: Lord of Blood
powers.desc: Heals HP of spellbound foes and also boosts attack power.

items.tagline: A bloodthirsty axe, counter-heals, and spellbound minions — win ugly, win long.
playstyle: Bloodhand Jan wants messy, close fights. The Bloodthirsty Axe hits hard and the Stone of Sorcery gives you a deceptive ranged option, but the real engine is counterattacking: Bloodhand Lineage restores HP when you trade after taking damage.
Blink is your get-out and your re-engage. Surrender to My Blood is a area-denial burst — plant the axe, flood the ground with blood slashes, and dare anyone to walk in.

tips.title: Trade on purpose
tips.desc: Do not panic-heal every chip. Counterattack after hits to trigger Bloodhand Lineage and stay in the pocket.

tips.title: Spellbind, then snowball
tips.desc: Lord of Blood heals spellbound foes and boosts your attack. After a successful blood drink, press the advantage instead of resetting.

tips.title: Blink is tempo
tips.desc: Use Blink to dodge a culling burst or to close after they waste stamina — the buff is temporary, so act fast.

lore: Jan’s epithet is not marketing. Bloodhand Lineage and Lord of Blood describe a fighter who treats blood as both wound and weapon — a theme FromSoftware loves to push until it turns romantic and ugly at once.
The axe that “thirsts” and the stone of sorcery place him between butchery and ritual: a Twilight mercenary who already knows the First Blood will be taken, not given.

items.name: Trang Lanh

bloodArts.name: Darkmoon
bloodArts.desc: Conceals the body behind the darkmoon for a limited period.

bloodArts.name: Mama Nātha
bloodArts.desc: Summons a giant silver serpent, the guardian of the Ratnam, to attack the surrounding area.

powers.name: Alluring Bride
powers.desc: Drinking blood also spellbinds nearby enemies.

powers.name: Daughter of the Darkmoon
powers.desc: Hides oneself from distant foes, and makes one harder for foes to target.

items.tagline: Darkmoon stealth, silver serpents, and alluring blood drinks — disappear, then decide the fight.
playstyle: Trang Lanh is an information fighter. Darkmoon conceals you for a short window — enough to break lock-ons, reposition, or open with a thrown Full Moon Blade. Mama Nātha is a wide-area summon that turns a duel into chaos.
Alluring Bride turns every successful blood drink into soft crowd control. Daughter of the Darkmoon keeps you hard to target at range, which is how you survive third parties in eight-player lobbies.

tips.title: Open from stealth
tips.desc: Do not show yourself first. Darkmoon in, throw the blade or start the summon, and let them panic into each other.

tips.title: Drink blood in crowds
tips.desc: Alluring Bride spellbinds nearby enemies on drink — stagger one target in a group and convert the whole skirmish.

tips.title: Stay at the edge of vision
tips.desc: Daughter of the Darkmoon is strongest when you are far. Creep the perimeter of fights instead of standing on the objective.

lore: The Full Moon Blade and Mama Nātha — a silver serpent guardian of the Ratnam — pull Trang Lanh toward myth rather than gothic Europe. The Twilight of Humanity is not only Victorian streets; it still keeps older gods and guardians in the dark.
Her Aspects frame her as bride and daughter of the darkmoon: a romantic, dangerous reading of blood power that fits Miyazaki’s stated interest in “romantic” blood rather than pure horror.

items.name: Sniper Layla

bloodArts.name: Neb-ra Vanishing
bloodArts.desc: Assume the form of a swarm of insects to move to a distant location. The afterimage confuses foes.

bloodArts.name: Verd Gatling Gun
bloodArts.desc: Extracts a giant Gatling gun from the wielder's body, prepares to fire, and then unleashes a rapid-fire barrage.

powers.name: Neb-ra Lineage
powers.desc: HP is gradually restored to 1/2 of max. A Goldblood Stake restores less than others'.

powers.name: Nighteye
powers.desc: Longer range for lock-ons and observation.

items.tagline: Insect-form repositions, a body-mounted Gatling, and Nighteye lock-ons — control the sightline.
playstyle: Sniper Layla owns the long angle. Nighteye extends lock-on and observation range, and the Sniper Rifle punishes anyone who rotates carelessly between Lowanro landmarks.

When the fight collapses on you, Neb-ra Vanishing turns you into a swarm and leaves a confusing afterimage. Verd Gatling Gun is your close-range panic button — or a brutal finisher if you set it up from high ground.

tips.title: Play elevation, not honor
tips.desc: Clock towers, roofs, and long streets are your kit. If you are in a tight corridor, you are playing someone else’s game.

tips.title: Vanish to reset, not to style
tips.desc: Neb-ra Vanishing is an escape and reposition tool. Use the afterimage to bait shots, then re-peek from a new angle.

tips.title: Respect the Stake economy
tips.desc: Neb-ra Lineage regenerates HP toward half, but Goldblood Stakes heal you less. Do not plan around burst heals.

lore: Hieroglyph Katars and a sniper rifle is a deliberate clash — archive and battlefield in one kit. Layla reads like a scholar-hunter whose bloodline (Neb-ra) is insectile and hard to pin down.
Nighteye and the swarm form make her the roster’s best “eyes”: in a game about culling and opportunism, information is a weapon as real as the rifle.

items.name: Senator Samir Patres

bloodArts.name: Bloodstake
bloodArts.desc: Form a swamp of blood at the feet of foes. A colossal bloodstake rises from the swamp.

bloodArts.name: Saurian Form
bloodArts.desc: Assume the form of a carnivorous dinosaur before charging at foes and attacking with powerful jaws.

powers.name: Unshakable Sword
powers.desc: Perfect guarding boosts melee attack power.

items.tagline: Senate rapier, blood swamps, and dinosaur charges — outbuild them, then run them over.
playstyle: Senator Samir Patres is a technical fighter who rewards clean defense. Unshakable Sword boosts melee attack after a perfect guard, so he wants structured duels more than brawls.

Blood Disciple lowers required Bloodsworn skill level — a quiet economy advantage that comes online earlier than opponents expect. Bloodstake locks space; Saurian Form is a shocking engage when they think you will keep fencing.

tips.title: Perfect guard is your damage buff
tips.desc: Train the guard counter window. Unshakable Sword turns defense into offense; do not mash dodge when you can parry.

tips.title: Spend the skill-level edge
tips.desc: Blood Disciple lets you take Bloodsworn skills earlier. Prioritize unlocks that compound (stagger, blood economy) over raw flair.

tips.title: Bloodstake then charge
tips.desc: Drop the swamp to pin them, then Saurian Form when they try to circle out of it.

lore: The title “Senator” and the Senate Rapier stage him as political aristocracy — until Saurian Form reminds you the Twilight still runs on monstrous blood, not speeches.
Bloodstake (a literal stake rising from a blood swamp) is ritual violence with legal theater around it. He is a strong read on the game’s tone: order, then something older and hungrier.

items.name: Zork

bloodArts.name: Missile
bloodArts.desc: Deploys a cannon from the back of the diving suit, assumes a firing stance, and then fires.

bloodArts.name: Human Rocket
bloodArts.desc: Deploys a propulsion mechanism from the back of the diving suit, shifting to flight mode and charging straight ahead.

powers.name: Law of the Deep Sea
powers.desc: Defeat Bloodsworn to steal max HP. Any HP gained is lost if defeated by a victim.

powers.name: Dread Resonance
powers.desc: A howl of inhuman sonic wavelength. Hold down [L] + [ZR] to extend howling.

items.tagline: Diving suit, speargun, rockets, and stolen max HP — be the problem they cannot ignore.
playstyle: Zork is a front-line menace. Undersea Cable and Speargun are honest tools, but Human Rocket and Missile make him the best character for forcing fights and breaking setups.
Law of the Deep Sea steals max HP on Bloodsworn kills — if you get ahead, you snowball. Dread Resonance is a howl you can extend to interrupt and inflate stagger; use it to ruin someone else’s combo.

tips.title: Kill to grow
tips.desc: Law of the Deep Sea wants Bloodsworn eliminations, not just PvE. Hunt players who are already weak from the Grail’s culling.

tips.title: Do not die to your victim
tips.desc: HP stolen is lost if the player you robbed finishes you. After a steal, reset or play safer — greed throws the lead.

tips.title: Hold the howl
tips.desc: Dread Resonance ([L] + [ZR]) extends while held. Use it to cancel telegraphed attacks or to bully a final-phase duel.

lore: A diving suit that grows cannons and rocket packs is peak Twilight industrial body-horror. Zork looks like deep-sea salvage and reads like a predator.
Law of the Deep Sea is a cruel rule set: take their maximum life, and lose it if they take yours. He is the network test’s meme favorite for a reason — and a real snowball threat in the final three.

intro.title: The Duskbloods Closed Network Test
intro.lead: The application period for FromSoftware's closed network test of The Duskbloods on Nintendo Switch 2 has ended. This page keeps the full schedule, requirements, and what participants actually played — useful context while we wait for the full 2026 release.

status.label: Applications Closed
status.desc: The network test application period has ended. Selected players were notified on August 7. If you missed this test, the practical takeaway is still valuable: the session structure, multiplayer pacing, and Switch 2 requirements below tell you exactly what to prepare for a future beta or the launch build. Bookmark this page — we keep it updated as official follow-ups appear.

application.label: Application Period
application.note: Repeated applications by the same user will be rejected. Participants will be selected by order of sign-up — early interest mattered more than profile polish.

selection.label: Selection Announcement
selection.note: Check your account page on the official site to find out the result. Selected players received a download code; if a future test appears, monitor the same account page rather than third-party rumor threads.

download.label: Client Download
download.date: Available from August 18 (Tues.) at 6:00 a.m. PDT
download.note: Selected players can use the download code on Nintendo Store or Nintendo eShop. In some regions, downloading via means other than Nintendo eShop is not supported.

sessions.label: Test Sessions
sessions.note: Session dates and times may change or be canceled without notice. The schedule deliberately used short windows across time zones — expect similar bursty sessions for any future test rather than a long open beta. If you plan around the next one, clear the full window rather than logging in for the last hour: matchmaking quality and lobby density were best at session start.

items.label: Region note
items.value: Some regions could not download outside Nintendo eShop

items.label: Save data
items.value: Enough free storage on Switch 2 for the test client

items.title: PvPvE structure
items.desc: Eight players compete across three rounds with mid-round culling. PvE pressure is constant, but the scoreboard is still written by player fights and objective control.

items.title: Short session windows
items.desc: Each test window was only a few hours. That rewarded players who had already learned Lowanro routes — practice the map in the final game the same way you would practice a raid night.

items.title: Virtue economy
items.desc: Virtue decides who advances and who is culled. The test made one lesson obvious: passive farming without contesting objectives is how you quietly lose.

items.title: Matchmaking feel
items.desc: Early reports suggested strong demand and busy lobbies. If a future test opens, expect queue pressure at session start — log in before the window, not at the buzzer.

items.title: Performance on Switch 2
items.desc: The test targeted native Switch 2 play, including handheld mode. Network stability mattered as much as combat skill during peak hours.

items.title: What transfers to launch
items.desc: Map knowledge, Virtue tempo, and compact/kin habits will carry forward. Weapons and exact balance numbers may change, but the decision loop will not.

items.title: How to use the test notes
items.desc: Rewatch your clips with the map open. Most improvement comes from noticing where you lost Virtue, not from mechanical flash — pathing is the skill check The Duskbloods actually grades.

items.title: What we are still waiting on
items.desc: An exact calendar date for the full release has not been confirmed. Until then, treat delay rumors as rumors and use this schedule as the last official multiplayer stress signal.

items.title: Team play vs solo queue
items.desc: You can queue alone, but coordinated pairs and trios controlled objectives more consistently. If a future test opens, line up at least one partner who knows the callout language of Lowanro before you queue.

cta.title: Stay tuned for the full release
cta.desc: The network test was a first look at The Duskbloods ahead of its planned 2026 launch on Nintendo Switch 2. Use the links below for launch timing, systems deep dives, and character prep — we update those pages whenever official details land. If you played the test, treat your notes as a head start: the players who already know Lowanro callouts, culling math, and kin breakpoints will hit the ground running.

intro.title: The Duskbloods — frequently asked questions
intro.lead: Straight answers to the questions players actually search: release date, Switch 2 exclusivity, PvPvE, single player, online requirements, and what the network test told us.

items.q: When does The Duskbloods come out?
items.a: The Duskbloods is officially scheduled for 2026 on Nintendo Switch 2. As of October 2026 an exact calendar date has not been announced. Trackers listing December 31, 2026 are placeholders, not confirmations.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods only on Nintendo Switch 2?
items.a: Yes. The Duskbloods is published by Nintendo and is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2 at launch. No other platforms have been announced.

items.q: Will The Duskbloods come to PS5, Xbox, or PC?
items.a: There are no announced plans for PS5, Xbox, or PC. As a Nintendo-published exclusive, it is expected to remain on Nintendo Switch 2.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods delayed to 2027?
items.a: Not officially. Nintendo and FromSoftware still list 2026. With no date in October and a crowded holiday calendar, a 2027 slip is widely discussed — but it has not been announced.

items.q: Is the December 31, 2026 release date real?
items.a: Unlikely. December 31 is a common year-end placeholder used by game databases when only the release year is known. Nintendo has not confirmed any calendar date.

items.q: How much will The Duskbloods cost?
items.a: No price has been announced. Expect details alongside the official release date and edition reveal.

items.q: Is there a physical copy or deluxe edition?
items.a: No edition lineup has been announced yet — not standard physical, not deluxe, not collector's. Those details usually drop with the date and pre-order page.

items.q: Can I pre-order The Duskbloods yet?
items.a: No. Pre-orders are not open. Treat any pre-order link that appears before an official Nintendo/FromSoftware announcement as unofficial.

items.q: What is the file size / install size?
items.a: Not announced. It will appear on the Nintendo eShop listing once the game page goes live.

items.q: What does PvPvE mean in The Duskbloods?
items.a: PvPvE means player-versus-player-versus-environment. In every match you compete against other Bloodsworn while also fighting powerful AI enemies — a three-way contest of rivalry, opportunism, and survival.

items.q: How many players can play together?
items.a: Up to eight Bloodsworn compete in a single Dusk Battle match. The match runs across four phases until only three finalists remain for the Blood Bestowal.

items.q: Can I play The Duskbloods single player?
items.a: Yes. Although multiplayer is the core, The Duskbloods includes a single-player mode so you can experience the systems without a full lobby.

items.q: Does The Duskbloods have crossplay?
items.a: Crossplay with other platforms does not apply — the game is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2. Multiplayer is among Switch 2 players.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods like Elden Ring Nightreign?
items.a: They share FromSoftware DNA and multiplayer-focused structure, but The Duskbloods is its own PvPvE design: 8-player matches, Virtue culling across phases, Bloodsworn builds, and a Switch 2 exclusive format directed by Miyazaki.

items.q: What is Virtue?
items.a: Virtue is the power you accumulate during a Dusk Battle. You bank it by fighting, exploring, and completing objectives. The Grail culls Bloodsworn with insufficient Virtue each phase — only the top three reach the final Blood Bestowal.

items.q: What are Blood Powers?
items.a: Special blood grants abilities beyond human limits. Up to five Powers of Blood can be manifested at once and swapped from the menu. They define much of how each Bloodsworn plays.

items.q: Is there skill-based matchmaking?
items.a: Yes. In an IGN interview, director Hidetaka Miyazaki confirmed a tiered, ranked-style matchmaking approach — new players should match with other newcomers rather than veterans.

items.q: Can I form alliances with other players?
items.a: Yes. You can petition rival Bloodsworn for an alliance, and Sigils create special relationship objectives. The network test also offered a Bloodbound Alliances mode where pairs stay bonded into the final phase.

items.q: Who are the Bloodsworn?
items.a: The playable characters. They are humans who gained superhuman power through special blood — conscious fighters with their own identity, weapons, abilities, and a customizable blood history.

items.q: How many playable characters are there?
items.a: Public reports say more than a dozen Bloodsworn. A full roster has not been published yet; more reveals are expected closer to launch.

items.q: What is blood history?
items.a: A customizable narrative element that shapes your Bloodsworn's path and destiny across a match. It gives each run room for personal build and story expression.

items.q: What are Kin and Compacts?
items.a: Those who enter an agreement with the Order of Dusk are known as kin. Compacts with Kin grant powers and progression (including Kin EXP) that strengthen your Bloodsworn during a battle.

items.q: What is the First Blood?
items.a: A mysterious force the Bloodsworn compete to obtain at the Twilight of Humanity. Pursuing it is the engine behind every match and the game's larger conflict.

items.q: Where does the game take place?
items.a: In the Lands of Dusk during the Twilight of Humanity — a dark, romantic world moving from gothic Victorian streets toward an industrial modern era. The network test staged matches in Lowanro City.

items.q: Who is directing The Duskbloods?
items.a: Hidetaka Miyazaki, president of FromSoftware and director of Elden Ring and the Dark Souls series. The game is developed by FromSoftware and published by Nintendo.

items.q: Was there a network test?
items.a: Yes. A closed network test ran August 21–24, 2026 across multiple sessions. Applications were held July 22–28, and selected players were notified August 7.

items.q: Do I need Nintendo Switch Online to play?
items.a: The closed network test required a Nintendo Switch Online membership. Expect online multiplayer in the full game to need it as well, though final requirements will be confirmed at launch.

items.q: Will there be another beta or network test?
items.a: Nothing has been announced after the August test. If a second test or open beta is planned, it will appear on official Nintendo/FromSoftware channels first.

items.q: How did the network test go?
items.a: Core gameplay impressed: PvPvE fights, Virtue culling, and Bloodsworn abilities landed well. Early sessions crashed under demand and PvP had lag, but FromSoftware patched mid-test and later sessions were more stable.

items.q: Does progress carry over to the full game?
items.a: Do not count on it. Network test progress is almost never carried into release builds. Official carry-over rules have not been published.

items.q: What is the House of Night?
items.a: The Bloodsworn base. There you choose characters, run tutorials and lessons, check records (weapons, Kin, items, Powers of Blood, events), practice on the Graveyard Scarecrow, and configure matchmaking.

items.q: What do I need to play The Duskbloods?
items.a: A Nintendo Switch 2 console. For multiplayer you should also expect a Nintendo Switch Online membership, based on the network test requirements.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods good for beginners?
items.a: It is approachable for newcomers, and Miyazaki has said matchmaking separates new players from veterans. The House of Night includes tutorials and practice. Expect a steep mastery curve past the basics.

items.q: Will there be a demo?
items.a: No public demo has been announced. The closed network test was the only hands-on opportunity so far.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods related to Bloodborne?
items.a: No. It is an original IP. The dark gothic tone invites comparisons, but The Duskbloods is not a Bloodborne sequel or spin-off.

items.q: Is this an official FromSoftware or Nintendo site?
items.a: No. This is an unofficial fan information site and is not affiliated with or endorsed by FromSoftware or Nintendo. Always confirm release details on official channels.

items.q: Does The Duskbloods have cross-save?
items.a: Nothing has been announced. The game is Switch 2 exclusive at launch, so cross-save with other ecosystems is not applicable unless Nintendo announces cloud save support details.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods a live-service game?
items.a: There are no announced seasonal battle-pass plans. It is a premium multiplayer action game from FromSoftware and Nintendo. Post-launch updates and balance patches are possible but not detailed yet.

items.q: How long is a typical match?
items.a: The network test structured fights across four phases of culling down to three finalists. Exact minute counts were not published — expect session-based matches rather than hour-long raids.

items.q: Where can I watch The Duskbloods gameplay?
items.a: Official trailers and network-test footage are on Nintendo and FromSoftware channels. Our gallery and newsroom break down what the footage shows.

items.q: What do I need to play The Duskbloods?
items.a: A Nintendo Switch 2 console. For online multiplayer you should also have a Nintendo Switch Online membership, based on the network test requirements. A Nintendo Account is required for the eShop and online play.

items.q: Is The Duskbloods on PC, PS5, or Xbox?
items.a: No. It is a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive. There is no PC version and therefore no PC minimum or recommended spec list.

items.q: Can I play without Nintendo Switch Online?
items.a: Single-player is available. Online multiplayer — the core eight-player Dusk Battles — is expected to require Nintendo Switch Online, as the closed network test did.

items.q: How much storage space do I need?
items.a: The install size is not announced yet. It will show on the Nintendo eShop listing. Plan for headroom beyond the base install for day-one patches.

items.q: Does it work in handheld mode?
items.a: Yes. Like other Switch 2 titles it supports TV, tabletop, and handheld play. Competitive multiplayer may be easier to read on a larger screen.

intro.title: About The Duskbloods
intro.lead: The Duskbloods is a PvPvE multiplayer action game from FromSoftware, directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and published by Nintendo for Switch 2 in 2026.

paragraphs: The project began from an encounter with Nintendo rather than an internal FromSoftware pitch. An embryonic collection of ideas was presented to Nintendo, who immediately expressed interest. The concept was originally conceived for the first Nintendo Switch, but the team delayed it to take advantage of the new Switch 2 hardware.

Set during the Twilight of Humanity — the end stage of civilization — the game centers on the First Blood, a mysterious force that the Bloodsworn compete to obtain. These are not classic vampires: Miyazaki has explained the concept deliberately departs from traditional vampire horror, drawing instead on the more romantic aspects of blood and power.

The Duskbloods is FromSoftware's first console-exclusive title in more than twenty years. Miyazaki has clarified that it does not interfere with the studio's single-player lineup, which continues in parallel with a separate team.

expect.title: About the launch
paragraphs: The Duskbloods was revealed during a Nintendo Switch 2 presentation and is slated for a 2026 release. As of October 11, 2026, FromSoftware and Nintendo still have not announced an exact calendar date. That is the single most important fact on this page — everything else is context around it.

As a Switch 2 exclusive, the game will only be available on Nintendo's current-generation console. It will not launch on PS5, Xbox, or PC. Multiplayer is built around Switch 2 players, and the network test required a Nintendo Switch Online membership.

Directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki (creator of Elden Ring and the Dark Souls series), The Duskbloods is a PvPvE multiplayer action game. Players take on the role of the Bloodsworn — warriors who draw power from special blood and compete for the First Blood at the Twilight of Humanity. Matches support up to eight players, with a single-player mode also available.

The August network test proved the core loop works: eight Bloodsworn enter the Lands of Dusk, bank Virtue, survive the Grail's culling across four phases, and fight down to a final three. It also exposed real server and netcode work still ahead of launch — which is exactly what a network test is for.

For buyers, that means two practical things. First, when the date lands, expect online multiplayer to want a Nintendo Switch Online membership — the test already required one. Second, do not trust any pre-order page, price tag, or calendar date that does not appear on an official Nintendo or FromSoftware channel. Placeholders and fake launch days have already circulated twice in this game's short public life.

window.title: Can it still make 2026?
paragraphs: Technically yes — and officially, 2026 is still the line. If the game ships this year, the realistic remaining windows are late November (unlikely against GTA 6) or December. A December 3 mid-week drop or a mid-to-late December date are the patterns fans and press keep pointing at.

In practice the calendar is brutal. A global multiplayer launch needs a marketing beat: date announce, pre-orders, maybe one more trailer, preload, then ship. Squashing that into a few weeks is possible but tight. If October and November pass without a date, a 2027 announcement becomes the rational expectation rather than pessimism.

What would settle it fast: a Nintendo Direct / Direct Partner Showcase featuring The Duskbloods with a locked date and pre-order date. Watch Nintendo's official channels and this page — we update the moment something is confirmed.

items.desc: Crouched close-up of the same silver-haired Bloodsworn: jeweled harness, wide cuffs, hair over one eye. In this game costume is data — house, lineage, and the blood craft you should respect. When a silhouette enters frame, you are already reading their kit.

items.title: Zork at the flooded shrine
items.desc: The diving-suit fighter sits in black water beside a mossy pale statue — swamp light, dead trees, a gate arch. Character vignettes like this whisper Compact and Kin themes without a tutorial. Slow frame in a fast game: worth a look before you queue.

items.title: Stairwell toad — PvE pressure on the route
items.desc: A katana user and a conical-hat hunter pinch a bloated red-eyed toad on a grand staircase. Readable maw, choke point, two angles: classic FromSoftware PvE geometry. These beasts are also resource nodes — Virtue, blood, and a third party you did not invite.

intro.title: Lands of Dusk — Lowanro City Map Guide
intro.lead: When a Dusk Battle begins, Bloodsworn are summoned to the Lands of Dusk. The network test stages every match on one land: Lowanro City — a multilayered field of landmarks, streets, and wilderness. This guide covers how the land is laid out, which regional features matter mid-match, and how to read the in-game map so you spend less time lost and more time banking Virtue before the grail's culling.

lands.title: The Lands of Dusk
lands.desc: One land, many layers. Lowanro is built as a vertical city-state: a clock-tower plaza anchors the center, a cathedral district watches the upper terraces, and outer streets dissolve into caves, forest, and lakeshore. Explore freely to strengthen your Bloodsworn and bank the Virtue you need to survive the grail's culling. Routes that look safe on the surface often hide third-party ambushes near chokepoints, so treat every landmark as both a resource node and a fight waiting to happen.

points.title: Lowanro City
points.desc: The network test's sole battleground — a city watched over by a towering clock tower and cathedral, with streets spreading around them. Expect frequent multi-team collisions in the plaza because it is the fastest path between spawn quadrants and several upgrade spawns.

points.title: Multilayered Regions
points.desc: Beyond the streets, the field branches into multiple regions including a cave, a forest, and a lake. Verticality matters: ledges, stairwells, and rooftops let short-range builds disengage while ranged Bloodsworn hold sightlines from above.

points.title: Revive Until You Fall
points.desc: You can revive any number of times in the Lands of Dusk — until you fail to survive the culling. Because lives are generous but the grail is not, dying late in a round is far more expensive than dying early while you still have time to rebuild Virtue.

points.title: Spawn Quadrants
points.desc: Players drop into distinct quadrants at match start. Early routing choices decide whether you contest a contested furnace, claim uncontested bloodbags, or sprint for golden spires that summon allies — each opening shapes the next two minutes of the round.

points.title: Culling Pressure
points.desc: After each round, the lowest-scoring players are culled. The map itself is neutral, but tempo is not: if you are behind, force fights near objectives instead of wandering the wilderness hoping for isolated PvE value.

points.title: Terrain Tells
points.desc: Look for ritual sites, teleport pads, and chains of light — they telegraph where players will cluster. Use the terrain as a scouting tool: if a region is quiet and empty, the real fight is usually on the other side of the clock tower.

regions.title: Regional Features
regions.desc: Several features appear in each region during a phase, and they change as the match advances. Check the map icons and pick the upgrades that fit your play style. A safe path is often the one that strings two features together without overcommitting to a three-team brawl in the plaza.

features.title: Bloodbag Elder
features.desc: Bloodsacs wander the land. Defeat them for blood crystals that enhance your Bloodsworn Skills. They are usually contested after the first culling, so secure a crystal route early instead of gambling on a late steal.

features.title: Alchemy Furnace
features.desc: Imbue weapons with fire and other affinities. Enhancing again at a matching furnace raises the weapon's enhancement level. Stacking a matching affinity is one of the few mid-round power spikes that is not tied to killing other players.

features.title: Kin Small Circles
features.desc: Small kin summoning circles appear — strengthen your compact and grant a large amount of experience to your partnered kin. Pair this with a safe farming loop if your kin is close to a breakthrough.

features.title: Golden Spires
features.desc: Golden spires can summon allies into the field. Treat them as high-value objectives: activating one under pressure often turns a losing skirmish into a stable fight, but standing in the open to channel is an invitation to third parties.

features.title: Ritual Sites
features.desc: Ritual Sites are where Sword Virtue is earned by killing players. If you are building an aggressive scoreline, path past them every phase; if you are protecting a lead, gatekeep the entrances instead of forcing the center.

features.title: Teleport Pads
features.desc: Teleport pads compress the map and punish slow rotations. Use them to escape collapses or to arrive first at a fading objective — then expect someone else to arrive three seconds later.

tools.title: Map Tools & Info Screen
tools.desc: Press [+] during a Dusk Battle to open the info screen and map. The map is your best scout when audio is noisy: it shows objective icons, teammate positions, and phase context without forcing you into a risky peek.

items.title: Live Objectives
items.desc: Track furnaces, circles, spires, and ritual sites as they appear. Icons update with the phase, so re-check after every round transition.

items.title: Team Positions
items.desc: See where your Bloodsworn partners are holding. If two teammates are already committed to the plaza, do not add a third unless you can finish the fight quickly.

items.title: Phase Context
items.desc: Culling windows and match structure reward different routes early versus late. Early rounds favor setup; late rounds favor closing on the final battle.

items.title: Quick Ping Habits
items.desc: Ping before you engage when possible. A one-second callout prevents the classic Lowanro mistake of winning a duel while the enemy team takes the spire behind you.

items.title: Sound Cues
items.desc: Roar conversions, flame arts, and ally summons are loud on purpose. Audio is information: if you hear a fight, decide whether to third-party or complete your own feature first.

items.title: Route Planning
items.desc: Before the gate opens, pick a two-feature loop. Wandering without a loop is how players fall behind on Virtue without realizing they never took a real fight.

intro.title: Kin — Compacts, Circles & Advancement
intro.lead: Kin are beings who struck a deal with the Order of Dusk. They enter compacts with Bloodsworn and lend their power in battle — a support layer on top of your weapons and Bloodsworn Skills. This page explains what compacts do, how the three summoning circles differ, which archetypes showed up in the network test, and how to grow or replace a kin mid-match without wasting the run.

what.title: Compacts with Kin
what.desc: Those who have entered an agreement with the Order of Dusk are known as kin. Kins enter compacts with the Bloodsworn, lending their power. Compacts are formed at summoning circles found at the base of the chains of light that stretch into the sky. In practice, a compact is both a combat partner and a second progression track: while you push your own Bloodsworn Skills, your kin quietly converts fight time into experience — so the partner you keep is as important as the weapon you carry.

circles.title: Summoning Circles
circles.desc: There are three types of kin summoning circle. Each one lets you compact with a different type of kin. Choosing a circle is a loadout decision disguised as a map decision: the circle family you bind first shapes which utility (sustain, control, or burst pressure) you can count on when the lobbies get crowded.

items.title: Ring
items.desc: A Ring-type summoning circle. Contracts with one family of kin — often the pick when you want reliable frontline support that can survive messy plaza brawls.

items.title: Blade
items.desc: A Blade-type summoning circle. Contracts with a different family of kin — typically more aggressive tools that help you convert skirmishes instead of stalling them.

items.title: Eye
items.desc: An Eye-type summoning circle. Contracts with yet another family of kin — utility-oriented partners that protect allies, reveal pressure, or punish overcommitted attackers.

circles.note: Eight kin exist in the network test version. Circle type limits which family you can bind, but every family still has multiple candidates — read the compact offer before you lock the run.

examples.title: Kin Archetypes
examples.desc: Various kin offer support with unique abilities. The network test included figures like these — none of them are cosmetic pets; each one changes how you should path, duel, and hold objectives.

items.title: Young Swordswoman
items.desc: A young swordswoman of a clandestine society. Reliable melee pressure that pairs well with aggressive Blood Arts and short rotations between ritual sites.

items.title: Flame Sorcerer
items.desc: A sorcerer who has mastered the flame. Excellent at denying chokes and finishing weakened targets after a furnace-imbued trade.

items.title: Singing Prisoner
items.desc: A prisoner who can protect allies by singing. Best when your team is stacking for spire channels or surviving a three-team collapse.

items.title: Black Wolf
items.desc: A black wolf who lords over a forest. Strong in outdoor lanes and forest edges, where chase tools and open sightlines decide who leaves the region.

items.title: Shield Bearer
items.desc: A stoic guardian who buys time. Use them when you need to stabilize after a bad culling instead of forcing another duel on low Virtue.

items.title: Lantern Scout
items.desc: A pathfinder who lights the way. Information-heavy kin that reward players who actually look at the map instead of autopiloting the plaza.

grow.title: Kin Advancement
grow.desc: When you defeat enemies while accompanied by a kin, your kin gains experience and can grow. Advancement is why mid-round farming still matters after your first weapon upgrade: every cleared bloodbag, staggered foe, and converted roar feeds the partner that will still be with you in the final three. Prioritize safe experience if your kin is one fight away from a breakpoint; prioritize score if the culling window is about to close.

summon.title: Summoning & Dismissing
summon.desc: Summon and dismiss kin from the Function menu. When kin die, you can summon them again after a cooldown, so a lost partner is a tempo hit — not a run-ender. Dismiss deliberately if a better compact becomes available and you can afford the downtime. The common mistake is clinging to a dead compact out of habit; the advanced habit is treating kin like any other cooldown-based advantage you re-evaluate between phases. Also remember that a compact is not a substitute for positioning: a kin can buy seconds, but it cannot fix a route that walks into three teams without a plan.

intro.title: The Duskbloods System Requirements — What You Need to Play
intro.lead: The Duskbloods is a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, so there is no PC spec sheet to chase. Here is what you actually need: the console, online membership for multiplayer, storage expectations, network, and accessories — confirmed vs. still unannounced.

platform.title: You need a Nintendo Switch 2
paragraphs: The Duskbloods is developed by FromSoftware and published by Nintendo as a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive. It does not run on the original Switch, and there is no PC minimum-spec table because there is no PC version — none announced for PS5 or Xbox either.

That means the only real “requirement” is Nintendo’s current hardware: a Nintendo Switch 2 console with enough free storage once the eShop listing goes live, and a display you are happy with in TV, tabletop, or handheld mode. The network test ran exclusively on Switch 2, which is the same target for launch.

If you already own a Switch 2, you are covered on hardware. If you are still deciding, watch for official bundles when the release date lands — Nintendo often pairs major exclusives with hardware SKUs.

online.title: Nintendo Switch Online for multiplayer
paragraphs: The closed network test required a Nintendo Switch Online membership to participate. Expect full-game online multiplayer — the eight-player Dusk Battles — to need the same. A Nintendo Account is required for the eShop and for online play.
Single-player is available without forming a full lobby, so you can learn systems offline. Crossplay does not apply: the game is Switch 2 only, so multiplayer is among Switch 2 players.

A stable broadband connection is strongly recommended. The August test showed early-session server load and PvP latency issues; a wired adapter or solid 5 GHz Wi‑Fi will feel better than a congested 2.4 GHz network.

storage.title: File size is still TBA
paragraphs: Nintendo has not published an install size yet. It will appear on the Nintendo eShop product page when the listing goes live with the release date and pre-orders.

As a practical floor, keep double-digit GB free on internal storage (or a fast microSD Express card for Switch 2) so preload and day-one patching are painless. Large multiplayer games often need room for the base install plus patches.

items.title: Joy-Con 2 / grip
items.desc: Full control support out of the box. Fine for handheld and casual TV sessions; combat timing may feel better with a full-size pad.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller
items.desc: Recommended if you plan to grind PvP. Sticks, triggers, and grip are more comfortable for longer Dusk Battle sessions.

items.title: TV mode
items.desc: Best for reading combat telegraphs and UI in multiplayer. 1080p/4K output depends on your TV and Switch 2 display settings.

items.title: Handheld mode
items.desc: Supported, as with other Switch 2 titles. Smaller UI can be harder in chaotic eight-player fights — use it for practice and House of Night time.
